overview.text: The Golden Tree Snake (Ornate Flying Snake) is a mildly venomous, rear-fanged tree snake of South and South-east Asia that can glide from tree to tree. It is harmless to people.

identification.text: Usually green with black cross-hatching and yellow or gold accents; flat head, narrow neck, blunt nose and big eyes with round pupils.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Malaysia, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, southern China and the Philippines.

behaviour.text: Active by day in trees and an excellent climber. It launches itself and flattens its body to glide between trees.

funfacts.text: It can 'fly': it flattens its body and glides from one tree to another.

recognise.text: Green and black with gold or yellow markings.
